title: Pilot-RCT: The Rasabox-Exercise in the treatment of Patients diagnosed with MDD.
summary:
This clinical trial aims to test the efficacy of Drama Therapy in the treatment of depression (DGPPN S3-LL Psychosocial Therapies, 2019). Drama Therapy is one of the four Arts Therapies (art, music, dance, and theater) acknowledged in Germany. The outstanding core feature of Drama Therapy is that it addresses social roles in an action-based approach to therapy (Frydman et al. 2022), which supports the client in dealing with their illness ("self-esteem enhancement"), (Kim & Moore, 2019). 
In Germany, "Drama Therapy" is yet to be implemented as a registered Master's program, therefore this is the 1st randomised controlled trial of a Drama Therapy intervention in Germany. In contrast, in some Anglo-American countries, Drama Therapy has been an academic subject for almost 40 years now. However, the field worldwide is so small that little clinical research has been conducted until today (Armstrong et al., 2019; Shafir et al. 2020; Chiang et al., 2019; de Witte et al., 2019; Emunah, 1983; Fancourt & Finn, 2019; Frydman et al., 2022; Sajnani, 2021). Therefore, in our study, we also draw on the body of literature on the antidepressant effects of activation in terms of physical exercise (Kandola et al. 2019; Gujral et al., 2017; Luttenberger et al., 2015; Mead et al., 2008). The physiological processes involved in both therapeutic procedures should be comparable. Also, current research on "embodiment in psychotherapy" (Danielsson & Rosberg, 2015; Rønberg, 2019; Fuchs & Koch, 2014; Lyons et al., 2021; Michalak et at 2018) seems to support our hypothesis that drama therapy (Sajnani, 2021; Landy, 1996; Goffman, 1959) is an effective procedure in depression treatment. In regard to our planned Drama Therapy intervention, an adapted version of the Rasabox Exercise will be applied. The intervention is highly structured and thus replicable. In the Rasabox Exercise, patients* engage with "8 emotional states" (Ekman, 1992; Ortony, 2022) in a spontaneous and creative way ("Becoming A Master of Emotions ", Ramesh, 2019; Schechner 2001; Sajnani & Gopalakrishna, 2017) and we will see if this intervention supports them in obtaining healthy emotion regulation stategies.

interventions.name: Intervention (wait list control group design): IG, 6 x Drama Therapy-Intervention ((2 x weekly, each session 90 Min. =>  20 Min. "Warm-up", 50 Min. "Action" (Rasabox Exercise), 20 Min. "Close-up")), then CG (Duration: 3 weeks), then Follow-up Phase (Duration: 3 weks). 4 points of meassurement: t0=ba
Wait List Control Group (wait list control group design): CG: Out- or inpatient treatment (depending on the setting), see Interventiongroup

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-sufficient german language skills
-status as patient (in- or out patient programs) with a cardinal diagnoses of MDD
Exclusion criteria:
-psychotic disorder (acute or lifetime), Schizophrenia, paranoid or schizoid type
-6 weeks sober on any illegal and legal drugs
- IQ < 85
